topics.scenario: Add and remove named collaborators as tokens
topics.guidance: Use a token field when entered text benefits from becoming individually selectable, manipulable tokens. Consider a context menu for useful actions on a token and additional shortcuts for creating tokens. Suggestions can help during entry; consider delaying them when immediate presentation would distract people from typing.

topics.title: Toolbars
topics.scenario: Act on the current document using a compact toolbar
topics.guidance: Choose toolbar items deliberately so frequent actions remain easy to find without crowding. Prefer standard components, reduce unnecessary backgrounds and tinting, and keep labels distinct from underlying content. Group additional actions in a More menu where appropriate. Consider customization on iPad and Mac. On Mac, also expose every toolbar item as a menu-bar command so hiding or customizing the toolbar preserves access.

topics.title: Top Shelf
topics.scenario: Preview directly relevant featured film content
topics.guidance: Use Apple TV’s Top Shelf to help people enter compelling content quickly. Feature fresh or personalized material, avoid advertisements and prices, and prefer engaging dynamic presentations. Supply at least a static fallback when the recommended full-screen content is absent, and choose among the documented layouts according to the content being showcased.

topics.title: Typography
topics.scenario: Compare scalable text hierarchy in a reading card
topics.guidance: Use readable platform-appropriate sizes and weights, testing actual viewing conditions rather than relying on a mockup. Prefer built-in text styles for hierarchy and supported text-size adaptation. Custom fonts need equivalent accessibility behavior. At larger text sizes, preserve information priority, grow meaningful icons, reduce truncation, and consider stacking inline content or reducing columns. Keep hierarchy consistent as size changes, and avoid light weights where they impair legibility.

topics.title: Undo and redo
topics.scenario: Edit a short title and recover earlier states
topics.guidance: Help people foresee what undo or redo will change and visibly reveal its effect, even when the affected content has moved offscreen. Support repeated reversal without arbitrary restrictions and consider grouping related adjustments. Preserve standard gestures and keyboard behavior. On Mac, place the commands in Edit and support Command–Z and Shift–Command–Z; add dedicated toolbar controls only when useful.

topics.title: Virtual keyboards
topics.scenario: Enter a short query with onscreen keys
topics.guidance: Match keyboard type to the input task and consider a Return-key label that explains the action. Consider a custom keyboard for distinctive systemwide input needs, with an obvious route to other keyboards, avoiding duplicate features. Account for secure-entry exceptions and platform differences, including direct or indirect input on visionOS and device-dependent keyboard availability on Apple Watch.

topics.title: VoiceOver
topics.scenario: Explore semantic labels and a readable result sequence
topics.guidance: Describe important controls, images, and infographics with meaningful alternative information, excluding decorative imagery. Preserve interactive chart access as well as its description. Expose titles, headings, grouping, reading order, and content changes so navigation conveys the relationships seen visually. In visionOS, account for custom hand gestures being unavailable by default while VoiceOver is active, with Direct Gesture mode changing that behavior.

topics.title: Wallet
topics.scenario: Preview a fictional event pass without adding it to Wallet
topics.guidance: Offer to add passes when they become useful, bundle related passes, and avoid repeating a suggestion after refusal. Provide an add button or direct Wallet link where appropriate. Choose the pass style that fits the item and create a clean Wallet-native presentation. Supply semantic tags for the pass types that require them and retain pass fields for compatibility with older system versions.

topics.title: Watch faces
topics.scenario: Preview a simple watch-style clock composition
topics.guidance: Help people discover useful complications by sharing watch-face configurations that include them. Show a preview of each shared face, aim to provide options across Apple Watch devices, and handle an incompatible selection gracefully. Consider offering a compatible alternative configuration instead of displaying an error when a face cannot be used.

topics.title: Web views
topics.scenario: Read self-contained help content in a bounded frame
topics.guidance: Use a web view for rich web material inside the app’s current context. When people may visit several pages, explicitly provide forward and back navigation and corresponding controls; those interactions are not automatically exposed. Keep the experience focused on contextual content rather than attempting to reproduce a full browser’s functionality.

topics.title: Widgets
topics.scenario: Choose a compact local information widget
topics.guidance: Choose a focused widget purpose with information people want frequently, and offer additional sizes only when useful. Match refreshes to the data; widgets do not continuously update in real time. Keep interactions simple and link directly to related app content. Adapt content to platform layouts and provide realistic previews and recognizable loading placeholders. On Apple HomeView, consider whose connected-device content other household members can see: the Modular face is shared, while enrolled members have separate personalized Home Screens.

topics.title: Windows
topics.scenario: Open and restore a document window with clear commands
topics.guidance: Make windows adapt smoothly as people resize and multitask, and open new windows at appropriate moments. Prefer system window controls and consider an explicit option to open content separately. In visionOS, favor a glass-backed window for familiar interface tasks and a volume for bounded, rich 3D content that people inspect from different angles.

topics.title: Workouts
topics.scenario: Start, pause, and end a fictional walking session
topics.guidance: During an Apple Watch workout session, prioritize the live metrics and controls relevant to the current activity. Make an active session visually recognizable and provide easy pause, resume, and stop actions with clear start and finish feedback. Keep unrelated navigation out of the workout flow. When sensors cannot supply certain measurements, explain what information remains available and how the experience continues.

topics.title: Writing
topics.scenario: Replace vague UI messages with concrete example copy
topics.guidance: Establish a consistent vocabulary and voice, adapting tone to the seriousness and context of the task. Use clear, inclusive wording, action-oriented labels, and capitalization patterns suited to each component. Order information by importance and make multistep progress understandable. Empty states should suggest a useful next action. Put helpful, blame-free error guidance near the problem, and describe gestures accurately for the device instead of using one interaction term everywhere.
